source_of_truth: The Planning Intelligence roadmap V0 scope: guide asks into roadmap vs implementation plan, surface parallel-ready work, and make release/documentation impact visible before dispatch.

user_journeys.name: new-user-turns-broad-ask-into-roadmap
user_journeys.description: A user asks DontPanic to improve product onboarding across install, dashboard, docs, and setup. The authoring guidance helps classify it as a tracking roadmap with child plans rather than one overloaded implementation plan.
acceptance_signals: Guidance explains why the ask is roadmap-shaped
Guidance shows how to name child implementation plans
Roadmap parent is not treated as the dispatchable implementation unit

user_journeys.name: operator-finds-parallel-work-without-reading-every-plan
user_journeys.description: An operator with several active plans runs dontpanic next and sees which features or child plans can safely be dispatched in parallel and which are blocked by dependencies or active overlap.
acceptance_signals: Ready work includes exact candidate commands
Not-ready work explains the blocking dependency
Active supervisor overlap is advisory and explicit
JSON output gives agents the same recommendation shape

user_journeys.name: author-catches-missing-public-doc-updates-before-merge
user_journeys.description: A plan changes README-facing or CLI-facing behavior. The release-impact checklist prompts the author to update the right public surfaces before the change merges.
acceptance_signals: Schema-only changes still point at claude/shared/CHANGELOG.md
Internal-only changes are not forced into public release notes

non_goals: No hard blocking on release-impact advisories
completion_test:
1. `dontpanic next --format=json` recommends independent ready work, suppresses dependency-blocked work with reasons, warns on active overlap without mutating state, and emits exact candidate commands where possible.
2. A new user reading docs/AUTHORING_PLANS.md can distinguish roadmap vs plan vs investigation vs setup.
3. Root CHANGELOG.md and release-impact guidance explain which documentation, onboarding, architecture, dashboard, CLI, schema, and social/discoverability surfaces need review for public-facing changes.
